purpose: Determine whether finite optimizer output, a nominal convergence code, or finite standard errors can be mistaken for existence of a finite CMLE on registered interior, boundary, and structurally unidentified additive-RSM controls; compare matched immer CMLE directly and treat mfrmr, TAM, and sirt as estimator-mismatched sensitivity analyses.

r_environment_before_execution.mfrmr_snapshot_rule: Install the current dirty 0.2.3 source into a new isolated temporary R library, then record package version, fit_mfrm function hash, source Git identity, status hash, and build-content hash before any fit. Never modify the source tree.

fixture_contract.source: Select exact unanchored cases from fixture_cases() without altering response bytes, declared category support, or expected status.
fixture_contract.matched_design: Person raw score is conditioned out; only sum-to-zero Rater effects and shared sum-to-zero RSM step parameters are free. Event/response-unit labels distinguish observations but are not estimated facets.
fixture_contract.excluded: PCM and hard-anchor cases require separate registered design-mapping and anchor-estimand studies and are not generalized from this run.

python_native.estimator: exact conditional maximum likelihood with pre-optimization finite-MLE support oracle
python_native.role: reference classification and matched numerical reference for interior cases
python_native.workflow_rule: Structural and boundary controls stop before optimization; only oracle-qualified interior cases are optimized.

immer.estimator: immer_cml with explicitly supplied matched design matrix, use_rcpp=FALSE, and declared-support zero-weight sentinel
immer.role: primary same-estimand numerical and boundary-behavior comparison
immer.interpretation: A returned finite coefficient vector or convergence code zero is not finite-MLE-existence evidence. Independent Python status remains authoritative for readiness in this experiment.

mfrmr.estimator: fit_mfrm JML from the isolated current 0.2.3 development snapshot
mfrmr.interpretation: Report fit return, warning, convergence/readiness fields, coefficient magnitude, and failure type; do not score equality to CMLE.

TAM.interpretation: Report observable termination and finite-output behavior; do not score equality to CMLE.

sirt.interpretation: Report observable termination and finite-output behavior; do not score equality to CMLE.

all_engines: maximum absolute estimate and standard error when extractable
immer_additional: analytic gradient sup norm and finite-difference disagreement
information rank, minimum eigenvalue, and condition number
behavior at maxit 200, 2000, and 10000 with reltol 1e-12
registered_observations.boundary_false_reassurance: For every Python boundary case, record separately whether immer returns code zero, finite coefficients, finite SEs, small gradient, and full-rank information. No single one of these flags may override the support-oracle boundary status.
registered_observations.binary64_sensitivity: Retain full-precision numeric outputs and compute classifications at gradient tolerances 1e-4, 1e-5, 1e-6, and 1e-8. Never base the primary result on printed or rounded coefficients, SEs, likelihood, fit indices, or MnSq.

success_gates.identity: All registered Python parents match; the installed mfrmr 0.2.3 snapshot matches all three registered source identities; all R function hashes and adapter hashes are retained.
success_gates.fixture_integrity: 13/13 exact case IDs, expected accounting 5/7/1, and response CSV byte hashes retained.
success_gates.python: 13/13 structured-workflow statuses match frozen expected status; optimization attempts are exactly five.
success_gates.immer_prefit: Python and independently reconstructed R conditional-information rank agree in 13/13; the structurally unidentified case does not reach immer optimization.
success_gates.immer_interior: All five interior cases return with optimizer code zero, finite coefficient/SE/loglik values, full information rank, and analytic gradient sup norm <= 1e-6 at maxit 2000.

immer_numeric.comparison_scope: five interior cases only, after exact parameter-name and sign-contract checks

success_gates.boundary_accounting: All seven boundary cases have complete multi-maxit ledgers even if immer reports nominal convergence. Boundary status is never overwritten by optimizer diagnostics.
success_gates.secondary_engines: mfrmr, TAM, and sirt each produce a complete 13-case attempt/error ledger. Fit success is descriptive and is not a pass/fail requirement because their estimands differ.
success_gates.tests: New contract tests and selected CMLE/workflow tests pass.

interpretation_limits.estimator_equivalence: Only Python native CMLE versus matched immer CMLE supports direct numerical comparison. TAM, sirt, and mfrmr results cannot establish CMLE parity or nonparity.
interpretation_limits.boundary_truth: The reference claim is existence of a finite optimum for the registered conditional likelihood, not correctness of the Rasch-family model or absence of data bias.
interpretation_limits.optimizer_limits: Iteration-cap drift and increasingly extreme finite estimates are symptoms to describe, not mathematical proof; the support oracle supplies the existence classification.
interpretation_limits.floating_point: R and Python optimizers, finite differences, eigenvalue ranks, and printed values use binary64 and tolerances. Exact discrete support maximization plus fail-closed LP tolerances is stronger but is not exact rational certification.
interpretation_limits.mfrmr_development: The current 0.2.3 source is dirty and unreleased. Evidence applies only to the frozen content hash and must not be presented as behavior of a future 0.2.3 release.
interpretation_limits.fit_metrics: This phase does not use MnSq to infer finite-MLE existence. MnSq rounding sensitivity remains a separate downstream decision layer.
interpretation_limits.generalization: No claim is made for PCM, anchors, sparse high-dimensional designs, bias tests, or public one-click UX from these 13 controls alone.
interpretation_limits.public_ui: withheld pending separate PCM/anchor comparison and user-comprehension review
